blocks.title: Repair Cafés
blocks.body:
In many towns in Europe, there are events called "repair cafés." At these events, people bring broken things such as lamps, clothes, and toasters. Volunteers who are good at fixing things help them repair the items for free.
The first repair café was started in the Netherlands in 2009. Its founder wanted to reduce waste. She noticed that people often throw things away ( 21 ). At a repair café, they can learn that many things can be used again after a simple repair.
Repair cafés are also good places to meet neighbors. While people wait, they can drink coffee and talk with each other. ( 22 ), repair cafés have spread to many countries around the world.

o: even when they could easily be fixed
because they want to help others
qs.ex: 直後に「簡単な修理でまた使えると学べる」とあるので、「簡単に直せるのに捨ててしまう」。
ごみが減る・近所の人と知り合えるという良い点を受けて「このため」世界に広まった、とつながります。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Daniel Moore
To: Riko Hayashi
Date: May 20
Subject: Science fair

Hi Riko,
Thank you for helping me with my science project last week. Thanks to your advice, I finished my poster about how plants grow in different kinds of light. Our teacher said it was one of the best projects in the class, so I was chosen to show it at the city science fair next month!
The science fair will be held at the city hall on June 14. Students from ten schools will show their projects, and judges will choose the three best ones. The winners will get a prize and a chance to visit a university laboratory.
I'm a little nervous because I have to explain my project to the judges in front of many people. Could you listen to my presentation this Saturday and give me some advice? My mother said we can practice at our house. She'll make pizza for us!
Your friend,
Daniel

qs.q: Why was Daniel chosen to show his project at the science fair?
o: He was the only student who finished a project.
His teacher thought his project was one of the best.
Riko asked the teacher to choose him.
He won a prize last year.
qs.ex: 先生が「クラスで最もよい作品の一つ」と言ったからです。

qs.q: What will the winners of the science fair get?
o: A chance to visit a university laboratory.
qs.ex: a prize and a chance to visit a university laboratory とあります。

qs.q: What does Daniel want Riko to do this Saturday?
o: Go to the city hall with him.
Make a poster for the fair.
qs.ex: Could you listen to my presentation this Saturday ～? とたのんでいます。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: A Train That Learned from Birds
blocks.body:
The Shinkansen, Japan's high-speed train, is famous for being fast and safe. However, when faster trains were developed in the 1990s, there was a problem. When a train entered a tunnel at high speed, the air in front of it was pushed out of the other end of the tunnel with a loud boom. People who lived near the tunnels complained about the noise.
An engineer named Eiji Nakatsu found an answer in nature. He was a member of a bird-watching club, and he knew about the kingfisher. This small bird dives from the air into water to catch fish, but it makes almost no splash. Nakatsu thought that the shape of the bird's long, thin beak might help a train move smoothly from the open air into a tunnel.
His team tested many shapes and designed a new nose for the train that looked like a kingfisher's beak. When the new train started running in 1997, the loud boom was gone. The train also used about 15 percent less electricity and became faster.
Nakatsu also learned from owls, which can fly very quietly. Their feathers have small edges that reduce noise, so his team used a similar idea for the part of the train that touches the power lines. Today, many engineers study animals and plants to find ideas for new technology.

qs.q: What problem did faster trains cause in the 1990s?
o: They made a loud noise when they entered tunnels.
They were too dangerous for birds.
qs.ex: トンネルに入るとき、出口で大きな音(トンネル・ブーム)が出ました。

qs.q: Why did Nakatsu think about the kingfisher?
o: It can fly faster than other birds.
It enters water with almost no splash.
It makes a loud sound when it flies.
qs.ex: カワセミは水しぶきをほとんど立てずに水に飛びこみます。

qs.q: What happened when the new train started running?
o: More people complained about the noise.
qs.ex: the loud boom was gone とあります。電気も約15%少なくなりました。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Nakatsu was a member of a fishing club.
The new train was first used in 2007.
Owls gave Nakatsu an idea for reducing noise.
qs.ex: 静かに飛ぶフクロウの羽を参考に、騒音を減らす工夫をしました。

parts.prompt:
あなたは、外国人の知り合い(Alex)から、Eメールで質問を受け取りました。この質問にわかりやすく答える返信メールを英文で書きなさい。
あなたが書く返信メールの中で、Alexのメールの下線部(new pet)について、あなたがより理解を深めるために、下線部の特徴を問う具体的な質問を2つしなさい。
返信は「Hi, Alex! Thank you for your e-mail.」で始まり「Best wishes,」で終わります(この部分は書かなくてよい)。
parts.body:
Hi!
I have some exciting news. My family got a [new pet] last week. It's really cute, and I play with it every day after school. But taking care of it is harder than I thought. Do you think it is good for children to take care of pets?
Your friend,
Alex
rules: 語数の目安は40語〜50語です。
Alexの質問に答えること、下線部(new pet)について質問を2つすることの両方が必要です。
parts.model: Yes, I think so. Children can learn to be responsible when they take care of pets. By the way, I want to know more about your new pet. What kind of animal is it? And what is its name? Please send me a picture.
checks: Alexの質問(子どもがペットの世話をするのはよいか)に答えている
答えの理由も書いている
new pet について具体的な質問を2つしている(What kind of animal…? What is its name? など)
語数が40〜50語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(Eメール)

parts.prompt:
あなたは、外国人の知り合いから以下のQUESTIONをされました。QUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。

QUESTION
Do you think people should read books more often?
rules: 語数の目安は50語〜60語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
QUESTIONに答えていない場合や、内容がQUESTIONからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I think people should read books more often. I have two reasons. First, reading books helps people learn many new words and ideas. Second, it is a good way to relax, because people can forget about their problems for a while. For these reasons, I think reading books is important.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
First, Second, For these reasons などで構成がわかる
語数が50〜60語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, Ben. You look happy today.
I got a part in the school play.
That's great! What role will you play?
items.ex: 何の役かと聞かれて役名を答えています。

lines: Excuse me. Can I use this coupon?
o: Here's a new one for next month.
items.ex: 期限切れのクーポンのかわりに来月分を渡しています。

lines: Dad, my bike has a flat tire.
Again? You just fixed it last week.
I know. Can you take me to the bike shop?
items.ex: 自転車屋に連れて行ってほしい→「いいよ、昼食のあとでね」。

lines: Are you going to the concert tonight?
I was going to, but I have a cold.
Oh no. Do you want me to sell your ticket?
items.ex: チケットを売ってあげようかと申し出られて「ありがたい」。

lines: Hello, this is Tony from Lake Hotel. You left a jacket in your room.
Oh, thank you! Can you send it to me?
items.ex: 住所を聞かれているので住所を答えます。

lines: Ms. Clark, I'm sorry I'm late.
The train stopped because of an accident.
items.ex: 電車が止まったという理由を聞いて「わかりました。すわって」。

lines: This soup is a little cold.
I'm very sorry. I'll bring you a new one.
Thank you. How long will it take?
items.ex: How long(どのくらい時間がかかるか)なので時間で答えます。

lines: I'm thinking of joining the tennis club.
items.ex: How often(どのくらいの頻度)なので回数で答えます。

lines: Do you know where Mr. Wilson is?
He's in a meeting until three.
Can I leave a message for him?
o: Sure. I'll give it to him.
items.ex: 伝言を引き受けています。

lines: What are you doing this weekend?
I'm going camping with my brother.
Sounds fun. Where are you going?
o: To a lake near Mt. Fuji.
items.ex: Where(どこ)なので場所を答えます。

lines: Hi, Mike. How was your trip to Kyoto?
It was great, but it was very crowded everywhere.
During Golden Week. Next time, I'll go in winter.
items.q: What will Mike do next time?
o: Go to Kyoto during Golden Week.
items.ex: Next time, I'll go in winter. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me. I ordered a cheeseburger, but this is a fish burger.
I'm very sorry. I'll make a cheeseburger right away.
Thanks. How long will it take?
About five minutes. You can keep the fish burger, too.
items.q: What will the man get?
o: A cheeseburger and a fish burger.
items.ex: チーズバーガーを作り直し、フィッシュバーガーもそのままもらえます。

lines: Mom, I want to learn the guitar.
That's nice. But guitar lessons are expensive.
My friend's brother can teach me for free.
items.q: Who will teach the girl the guitar?
o: A teacher at a music school.
items.ex: 友達のお兄さん(弟)が無料で教えてくれます。

lines: Hi. I have an appointment at three today, but I need to change it.
Sure. How about tomorrow at ten?
items.q: When will the woman go to the clinic?
items.ex: 予約を明日の10時に変更しました。

lines: Did you finish the history report?
Not yet. I still need to find more information.
The city library has a lot of books about history.
Thanks. I'll go there after school.
items.q: What will the girl do after school?
items.ex: I'll go there(市の図書館)after school. と言っています。

lines: Tom, can you help me move this sofa?
Sure. Where do you want to put it?
Next to the window. I want more light when I read.
items.q: Why does the woman want to move the sofa?
o: To get more light when she reads.
To make room for a TV.
items.ex: I want more light when I read. と言っています。

lines: Are you ready for the trip tomorrow, Lisa?
Almost. But I can't find my passport.
Did you check your desk drawer?
items.q: Where was Lisa's passport?
items.ex: 机の引き出しを見たらありました。

lines: Excuse me. How much is a ticket to the aquarium?
It's twenty dollars for adults and ten dollars for students.
I'm a student. Here's my student card.
items.q: How much will the girl pay?
items.ex: 学生は10ドルです。

lines: I'm thinking of buying an electric car.
They're good for the environment, but they're expensive.
Yes, but I'll save money on gas.
items.q: What does the woman say about electric cars?
o: They use a lot of gas.
items.ex: they're expensive と言っています。

lines: Grandma, I'm going to the store. Do you need anything?
Could you buy some eggs and milk?
Oh, and some bread for tomorrow's breakfast.
items.q: What will the boy buy for his grandmother?
items.ex: 卵と牛乳、そして明日の朝食用のパンをたのまれました。

lines: Mark loves soccer, but last month he hurt his leg during a game. The doctor told him not to play for two months. Now he goes to watch his team's games and helps the coach. He is looking forward to playing again.
items.q: What does Mark do now?
o: He helps the coach at games.
He goes to the hospital every day.
items.ex: チームの試合を見に行き、コーチを手伝っています。

lines: Welcome to Sunny Department Store. Today only, all shoes on the fourth floor are 30 percent off. Also, customers who spend more than 50 dollars can get a free gift at the information desk on the first floor.
items.q: What can customers who spend more than 50 dollars get?
items.ex: can get a free gift at the information desk とあります。

lines: Anna moved to Japan from Brazil last year. At first, she couldn't read Japanese, so shopping was difficult. Then her neighbor started teaching her hiragana. Now Anna can read many signs and enjoys shopping alone.
items.q: Who taught Anna hiragana?
items.ex: her neighbor started teaching her hiragana とあります。

lines: Octopuses are very smart animals. They can open jars to get food, and some can even use coconut shells as a place to hide. Scientists think that octopuses can remember things for a long time.
items.q: What can some octopuses do?
items.ex: some can even use coconut shells as a place to hide とあります。

lines: Attention, please. Because of strong winds, the ferry to Green Island will not run this afternoon. Passengers with tickets can get their money back at the ticket office or use their tickets tomorrow.
items.q: Why will the ferry not run this afternoon?
o: Because of a problem with the engine.
items.ex: Because of strong winds とあります。

lines: Yuta wanted to become a better speaker of English, so he started recording himself every night. He listens to the recordings and finds his mistakes. His teacher says his pronunciation has improved a lot.
items.q: What does Yuta do every night?
items.ex: 毎晩、自分の英語を録音しています。

lines: Helen works at a zoo. Her job is to take care of the giraffes. Every morning, she gives them leaves and cleans their house. This spring, a baby giraffe was born, and many visitors come to see it.
items.q: What happened this spring?
o: Helen started working at the zoo.
items.ex: This spring, a baby giraffe was born とあります。

lines: Good afternoon, students. The school library will be closed next week because new bookshelves will be put in. During that time, you can borrow books from the classroom on the second floor.
items.q: Where can students borrow books next week?
o: From a classroom on the second floor.
items.ex: 2階の教室で本を借りられます。

lines: Last summer, Mr. Sato's family planned a trip to the beach. But on the day of the trip, it rained heavily. Instead, they went to an indoor pool. The children enjoyed the water slides very much.
items.q: Where did Mr. Sato's family go?
items.ex: 雨だったので屋内プールに行きました。

lines: Many people in Japan use furoshiki, a square piece of cloth, to wrap things. Furoshiki can be used again and again, so some stores now give them to customers instead of plastic bags.
items.q: Why do some stores give furoshiki to customers?
o: They can be used again and again.
items.ex: can be used again and again(何度も使える)とあります。
